name: Mount Everest
headline: height
subtitle: Sagarmatha / Qomolangma, Nepal-China border
description: Mount Everest, on the border between Nepal and China, is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level. A Nepali survey team measured the summit in 2019 and a Chinese team in 2020, and on 8 December 2020 the two countries jointly announced a height of 8,848.86 m (29,031.69 ft). The figure includes the snow and ice on the summit, and the National Geographic Society has adopted it as Everest's official height.

measures.label: Height above sea level
measures.note: Summit height including snow and ice cover; joint Nepal-China measurement announced 8 December 2020

facts.text: National Geographic reports the jointly announced height as 29,031.69 feet above sea level.
The height was announced on 8 December 2020 in a joint statement by the Survey Department of Nepal and Chinese authorities.
The National Geographic Society adopted the new figure, which includes the summit's snow and ice cover, as Everest's official height.
The Nepali survey team summited on 22 May 2019 to place a GPS receiver; a Chinese survey team measured from the north side in spring 2020.

The height was announced at the same time in Kathmandu and Beijing, at an event attended by Nepal's foreign minister Pradeep Gyawali and China's foreign minister Wang Yi; a separate 'rock height' was not announced.
The previously accepted height was 8,848 metres (29,028 feet).

caveats: Britannica refused automated access (HTTP 403), so the figure comes from The Kathmandu Post's report of the official announcement, cross-checked against National Geographic's feet figure (29,031.69 ft).
The height includes the summit snow and ice cap; the underlying rock height was not announced.
The mountain outline is illustrative; only its height above sea level is to scale.
